purpose: Concept refinement for discussion; full-height rear shield, short wraparound side wings, fully extended deployed wings. Production implementation remains paused.
initialPrompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Revise the shield-wall design for Trackstorm by combining the two reference concepts selected by the user.
Reference 1 DOZER: use its construction machinery weight, thick scraping lip, chipped ochre yellow steel, reinforcing ribs, hinge pins and exposed mechanical braces.
Reference 2 IRONCLAD: use its faceted armor, angular shoulders and shallow welded chevron reinforcing ridge. Keep the battered red armored off-road Car and the hand-drawn industrial concept-art language consistent with the references.
User's new requirements are the priority:
1. The MOUNTED REAR SHIELD must cover the FULL HEIGHT of the vehicle: from just above road level (small functional ground clearance) all the way to the roof/roll-cage top. It is dramatically taller than the low rear plates in the references. It shields the tires and body in a straight rear elevation. Do not leave the roof exposed above it. Keep the car its original size; enlarge the shield.
2. A full-height hinged wing on EACH side wraps FORWARD along a SHORT portion of the vehicle's rear sides, forming a U-shaped protective shell around the rear quarter. These wings are visibly perpendicular to the broad rear center panel in mounted mode, outside the rear tires with clearance, extending forward roughly to the middle/front of the rear wheel region, not along the whole vehicle. They are side protection, not tiny outward fins or folded flat panels behind the center.
3. On deployment, those SAME two wings swing OUTWARD about vertical hinges until FULLY EXTENDED left and right, COPLANAR with the central plate: a straight wide continuous wall in plan, wings no longer wrapped forward or held at 45 degrees. Same panel heights, same material, same panel count in both states. No enlargement by magic. Full-height center plus two full-height side panels. Clear readable swing arrows in the small plan-view diagram.
Design: a blunt aggressive industrial shield with a broad central panel, very shallow peaked/angled upper edge, thick dark structural frame, ochre armor plates, welded angular chevron rib inspired by Ironclad, bolted replaceable blackened scraping edge inspired by Dozer. Lower edge mostly straight, no deep spear point. Large simple surfaces and a few purposeful ribs, dents and exposed-metal wear. No gravestone motifs, arches, fantasy glow, guns, spikes or invented new gameplay mechanics.
Compose ONE wide landscape development sketch sheet on off-white paper. Title exactly "DOZER x IRONCLAD". Main left view: rear three-quarter view of the red Car wearing the tall U-shaped shield, viewed slightly above so the near wing clearly wraps FORWARD around the rear side and the car front is visible beyond it; tall rear shield should obscure the rear body. Main right view: detached deployed shield as a broad straight freestanding wall in three-quarter perspective, both wings fully open. Keep the shield panel height consistent relative to vehicle scale across views. Underneath add a small pure REAR ELEVATION establishing roof-to-near-road coverage and a very clear TOP VIEW sequence showing [car nose upwards, U-shell around rear] -> [detached straight line of three panels], label "WINGS WRAP FORWARD" and "WINGS OPEN FLAT". Label main views "MOUNTED — FULL HEIGHT" and "DEPLOYED — FULL SPAN". Render as expressive professional pencil/ink design sketch with muted color washes, not photorealistic; no extra concept variants on the page.
This is a concept refinement for discussion, not an engineering-certified fit drawing.
refinementPrompt:
Edit the supplied DOZER x IRONCLAD concept sheet with exactly one correction: in the LARGE TOP-RIGHT DEPLOYED drawing, straighten both wing panels so the three panels form one continuous FLAT WALL, all in the SAME PLANE, with no wrapping, inward toe-in, curvature or angled side panels. The bottom scraping edges across all three panels must lie on one straight perspective baseline; the left and right wing planes must share the same perspective vanishing point as the central panel. A nearly frontal view is acceptable to make fully straight extension unmistakable. Retain exposed vertical hinges at the seams and keep all three panels full height with the same yellow steel, chevron central reinforcement and black lower lip.
Everything else stays unchanged: title, left mounted drawing with tall wings wrapping FORWARD around the car's rear sides, the rear elevation, bottom mounted U-shaped top view and bottom deployed straight-line top view, hand-drawn style, layout and labels. Do not shorten the mounted shield; retain near-ground-to-roof height. Do not add panels or objects. The exact correction is fully flat and coplanar deployed wings.
